You are adding translations (i18n) to the home page panel of a Next.js 16 app ("Heard": live captions for YouTube livestreams). Repo: /Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions, web app in apps/web. Other agents are editing OTHER files at the same time; only edit the files listed as yours. Do not commit, stash, reset or switch branches.

The i18n setup is already built (read these first, do not change them):
- apps/web/src/i18n/config.ts (locales en, es, fr, pt, de, ja)
- apps/web/src/i18n/I18nProvider.tsx: client hook `useT("home")` returns the current language's object for the "home" area, e.g. `const t = useT("home"); t.hero.title`.
- apps/web/src/i18n/messages/en/common.ts and es/common.ts show the pattern: English file exports a plain object; each other language file does `import type { home as en } from "../en/home"; export const home: typeof en = {...}` so TypeScript forces the same shape. Functions are allowed for interpolation, e.g. `jumpTo: (time: string) => \`Jump to ${time}\``.

Your files:
- apps/web/src/components/HeroPanel.tsx (the header/nav part already uses `useT("common")`; leave that. Translate everything else: HomeTab, TabBody uses, HowTab, PrivacyTab incl. its art pieces' visible words, ExtensionTab titles/intro/footer, Terminal's "Copy"/"Copied" and its aria-label, the EXAMPLES `detail` text (keep channel names like "Ms Rachel" and "Sky News" as is), "Or try one", etc.)
- apps/web/src/components/StepArt.tsx (small illustration labels like "Start captions", "This tab", "Window", "Screen", "Also share tab audio", "Cancel", "Share". Note: the picker labels mimic Chrome's own dialog; translate them the way Chrome's UI reads in that language if you know it. Also CAPTURE_STEPS titles/bodies there; check where CAPTURE_STEPS is used (grep) — if it's used by StartGuide.tsx, which belongs to another agent, keep exporting CAPTURE_STEPS unchanged in shape but do NOT translate it; just translate the art components.)
- apps/web/src/components/UrlForm.tsx (placeholder, button, errors, labels)
- apps/web/src/i18n/messages/{en,es,fr,pt,de,ja}/home.ts (currently empty objects `{}`; fill them)

Rules:
- Translate only the site's UI words. Never translate terminal commands, paths, URLs, "Heard", "Deepgram", "YouTube", "Chrome", channel names.
- Write natural, concise UI copy in each language (Spanish neutral Latin American, Portuguese Brazilian, Japanese polite but short). Keep the same meaning and tone as the English. No em dashes in English copy.
- Keep the English text exactly as it is today (just moved into en/home.ts).
- Components are client components ("use client"); StepArt may not be — add "use client" if you need the hook there, or pass labels in as props from the caller.
- Watch for layout: German and French run longer. If a short label is in a tight spot (illustrations), prefer a shorter wording.
- When done run: cd apps/web && PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.1/bin:$PATH npx tsc --noEmit -p .  (the node on PATH by default is broken; always use that PATH prefix). Other agents may cause unrelated type errors in their own files; only fix errors in yours.
- Do NOT start or stop the dev server.

Report back: the list of files changed, any strings you deliberately left in English and why, and the tsc result.

content.text:
I've translated the home page panel into es, fr, pt, de and ja. The tsc check passes with no errors. I didn't open the page in a browser, so nothing is checked visually yet, including how the longer German and French text fits.

**Files changed:**
- `/Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions/apps/web/src/i18n/messages/en/home.ts` now holds all the English text, unchanged. `es`, `fr`, `pt`, `de` and `ja` `home.ts` in the same folder follow the same shape.
- `/Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions/apps/web/src/components/HeroPanel.tsx`: everything except the header uses `useT("home")`. That covers HomeTab, the example details, "Or try one", HowTab, PrivacyTab and its pictures, ExtensionTab, the Terminal copy button and its aria-label, and the "Watch" button in the paste picture. The aria-label is now a function, `copyLabel(lines)`, so each language can order the words its own way.
- `/Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions/apps/web/src/components/StepArt.tsx`: I added `"use client"` so the three pictures can use the hook. `CAPTURE_STEPS`, which `StartGuide.tsx` uses, keeps its shape and its English text.
- `/Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions/apps/web/src/components/UrlForm.tsx`: the label, placeholders, buttons and errors are translated.

**Error messages in the link box:** they're written in English in `lib/providers`, which isn't one of my files. So `localizeError()` in UrlForm spots the three link errors by how their English text starts and swaps in the translation:
- "Paste a full video link…"
- "Heard doesn't recognize…"
- "Channel links…"

If someone rewords those in `lib/providers`, the box falls back to the English text. A cleaner fix would be for providers to return an error code instead.

**Left in English on purpose:**
- `CAPTURE_STEPS` titles and bodies, as you asked.
- Channel names, terminal commands, paths and URLs, plus "Heard", "Deepgram Nova-3", "README", "Chrome", "Edge" and "YouTube".

**Shorter wording in the small pictures:**
- "Start captions" is "Sous-titrer" in French.
- The audio switch is cut down in every language, for example "Compartir audio", "Partager l’audio", "Tab-Audio teilen" and "タブの音声も共有".
- The French How tab step reads "Cliquez sur Sous-titrer" to match the button in the picture. If the real start button on the watch page is translated differently, the two should be made to match.
